key_insight: Incorporating mask priors into denoising diffusion models lets the generator respect known residue constraints and structural motifs, producing more accurate and diverse amino-acid sequences for a target protein backbone.
problem_solved: Inverse protein folding—designing amino-acid sequences that reliably fold to a given 3D backbone—is hard because sequence space is vast, constraints (fixed or uncertain residues) must be respected, and conditional generative models struggle to balance accuracy and diversity.
method: Use a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) to generate protein sequences conditioned on a target backbone.
Introduce mask priors that encode fixed/known residues or regions of uncertainty; inject these priors into the diffusion denoising steps to guide sampling and preserve constraints.
Train and evaluate the model to optimize sequence recovery, structural compatibility, and generation diversity under masked constraints.
impact: Provides a practical, constraint-aware generative framework for computational protein design: improves sequence accuracy and controllability, enabling better downstream experimental testing and integration into protein-engineering pipelines.
visual_elements: Schematic of the denoising diffusion process with an overlaid mask prior guiding each denoising step (flow diagram from noisy sequence to clean sequence).
Before/after backbone-to-sequence examples showing how masked residues are preserved and how generated sequences differ when mask priors are used vs. not used.
Bar/line charts comparing metrics (sequence recovery, RMSD or structural compatibility, and diversity) across baseline methods and the mask-prior-guided model.
Architecture diagram highlighting how backbone features, mask priors, and diffusion states are fused during denoising.
paper_title: Author Correction: Mask-prior-guided denoising diffusion improves inverse protein folding
paper_authors: Peizhen Bai, Filip Miljković, Xianyuan Liu, Leonardo De Maria, Rebecca Croasdale-Wood
